editionNote: Evening edition. It covers the 24 hours to 17:10 CET on 1 November; new research covers 05:10 CET to 17:10 CET on 1 November, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Russia Launches 433 Drones Overnight as Ukraine's Power Grid Takes New Hits
items.lede: Strikes on energy sites left hundreds of thousands of families without power, and a Sunday drone strike in Vinnytsia region killed two people.

sections.text: Russia launched 433 strike and decoy drones at Ukraine from 18:00 Kyiv time on Saturday (17:00 CET), the Air Force said [1][2]. The total included 64 jet-powered Shaheds [1]. By 07:30 Kyiv time on Sunday, air defenses had shot down or jammed 371 drones, and more than 40 were still airborne [1][2]. Drones hit 16 locations, and debris fell at 14 more [1][2]. Russian attacks over the past day killed one person and injured at least 47, regional officials said [2]. Zelensky said hundreds of thousands of families were without power and urged allies to speed up air defense decisions [2]. DTEK imposed emergency power outages in Kyiv after the overnight strikes [2]. On Sunday afternoon, a Russian drone hit near a vocational school dormitory in the Koziatyn community of Vinnytsia region [3]. The strike killed a man and a woman and injured two 5-year-olds and a 16-year-old boy, regional officials said [3]. No Russian Defense Ministry statement on the strikes on Ukraine was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is moderate on the drone totals, because they are the Air Force's own preliminary figures carried by two outlets. Confidence is high on the casualties, which regional officials and emergency services reported on record.

items.title: Russia's FSB Detains a Minor Over the Moscow Park Threat the US Flagged
items.lede: Russian security officials credited the American tip, saying the suspect posted armed TikTok photos at Tsaritsyno; a concert there was canceled and no attack occurred.

sections.text: The US Embassy in Russia said on Saturday it was aware of a credible threat of a mass-casualty event that day at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow [4][5]. It said the US government was coordinating a response with Russian authorities and told people to avoid the area [5][6]. Russia's FSB security service told state media it had received information from US partners about a planned terrorist attack and was taking action [5][6]. The park was evacuated during a concert and closed, Russian media reported [5][7]. On Sunday, the FSB said it had checked the US information and detained a Russian minor [7][8]. It said he posted TikTok photos of himself in tactical gear holding what looked like a rifle [7][8]. His posts included photos taken at Tsaritsyno with the caption "I found a place," the FSB said [8]. The FSB said his phone showed a neo-Nazi Telegram subscription and searches about mass shootings [7][8]. It said planned public events at the park were canceled, and it thanked the US side [8]. No attack or casualties were reported by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the embassy warning and the detention, which NBC News, Reuters, and Interfax quote on record. The suspect's posts rest only on the FSB's account.

items.title: Zelensky Says Ukraine Also Hit $70 Million in Russian Air Defenses
items.lede: Kyiv's president said the strikes hit a Pantsir-S2 and an S-400 command vehicle and credited the Security Service of Ukraine for the Rostov-region plant attack.

sections.text: Ukraine's General Staff said its forces struck the Kamensky Combine in Kamensk-Shakhtinsky, in Russia's Rostov region, on the night of 30–31 October [9][10]. It said strike drones and the Navy's Neptune coastal missiles were used [9]. The General Staff said a warehouse of finished goods caught fire and four production workshops were damaged [9][10][11]. It said the plant makes solid rocket fuel for Uragan, Smerch, and Tornado-S rocket launchers and for other missiles [9]. On Sunday, President Zelensky said the Kamensky Combine is involved in Russian missile production [12][13]. He said Ukrainian forces also hit a Pantsir-S2 air defense system and a command vehicle of an S-400 Triumf system [12][13]. He put the value of the air defense assets hit at about $70 million [12][13]. He thanked the Security Service of Ukraine and other units for the strikes [12][13]. No Russian official comment on the plant was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate. Reuters, DW, Ukrinform, and Ukrainska Pravda carry the Ukrainian claims, but the damage and the dollar value rest on Kyiv's own account with no independent confirmation.

items.title: Russian Governor Reports Heavy Damage at a Kstovo Plant After Drone Raid
items.lede: Nizhny Novgorod's governor did not name the site, but monitoring channels identified Lukoil's NORSI refinery, which supplies fuel to Russia's military.

sections.text: Lukoil's NORSI oil refinery in Kstovo, in Russia's Nizhny Novgorod region, was reportedly hit by drones overnight into Sunday, the Kyiv Independent reported [14]. Ukrainian monitoring channels Exilenova+ and Supernova+ posted footage of the alleged attack [14]. Independent Russian outlet ASTRA said the refinery was struck and burning [14]. NORSI, Russia's fourth-largest refinery, processes about 15 million to 17 million metric tons of crude a year [14]. It sits about 800 kilometers (500 miles) from Ukraine's border [14]. The plant supplies fuel to Russia's armed forces and the Moscow region [15]. On Sunday morning, Nizhny Novgorod Governor Gleb Nikitin said a massive drone attack caused significant damage to an industrial facility in the Kstovo district [15][16]. He did not name the facility and said more than 100 drones were destroyed, with no casualties reported [15][16]. Nikitin warned of temporary power, hot water, and heating cuts in some homes during repairs [16]. Russia's Defense Ministry said air defenses shot down 235 drones nationwide overnight [15]. No Ukrainian military statement on the refinery was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that a site in the Kstovo district was damaged, because the regional governor said so on record. Confidence is moderate that it was the Lukoil refinery, which rests on monitoring channels and ASTRA relayed by three outlets.

items.title: Kremlin Wants Only the US, Russia, and Ukraine at the First Abu Dhabi Rounds
items.lede: Zelensky has floated November 6 to 10 for the meeting, while a top Putin aide cited Moscow's direct contacts with Washington to keep Europeans out of early rounds.

sections.text: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Friday that preparing for three-way talks on Ukraine in Abu Dhabi does not commit Russia to limit fighting [17]. The Kyiv Independent, citing an unnamed senior Ukrainian official, reported that Kyiv suspects Moscow of offering a phone call to avoid an in-person leaders' meeting [18]. Late Friday, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told a news conference in Atlanta that if Zelensky wants to meet Putin, he can come to Moscow [19]. Late Saturday, Zelensky told US interviewer Tony Perkins that the three-way meeting could take place between November 6 and 10 [20]. He said Abu Dhabi was the tentative venue, but neither the dates nor the place were final [20]. He said Ukraine backs the US proposal for technical-level talks [20]. On Sunday, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said at least the first rounds should include only Russia, Ukraine, and the United States [21]. He was asked about European involvement and cited Moscow's working contacts with the Americans [21].

Confidence is high on Peskov's, Lavrov's, Zelensky's, and Ushakov's statements, which Interfax, the Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, and Reuters carry on record. The dates are tentative by Zelensky's own account. Kyiv's suspicion of a phone-call ploy rests on one outlet and an anonymous official.

items.title: Russia Sends 168 More Drones at Ukraine in a Daytime Saturday Wave
items.lede: The overnight raid of 134 drones was followed by a daylight barrage, and falling debris injured a 12-year-old girl at a Kyiv mall.

sections.text: Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 134 attack drones from 18:00 Kyiv time on Friday 30 October (17:00 CET) [22]. It said 72 of the Shahed drones were jet-powered, and Gerbera and decoy drones were also used [22]. As of 08:30 Kyiv time (07:30 CET) on Saturday, air defenses had shot down or jammed 105 drones [22][23]. Drones hit 20 locations, debris fell at 10 more, and several drones were still in the air [22]. From 06:30 to 19:30 Kyiv time on Saturday, Russia launched 168 strike drones and S8000 Banderol missiles, the Air Force said [24][25]. Air defenses shot down or jammed 122 drones and two Banderol missiles, and about 30 drones were still airborne [24][25]. In Kyiv, drone debris fell at a shopping center in the Obolonskyi district and injured a 12-year-old girl [26]. Later, a drone crashed in an open area in the Darnytskyi district, city officials said [27].

Confidence is moderate on the totals, because they are the Air Force's own preliminary figures, though at least two Ukrainian outlets carry each tally. Confidence is high on the Kyiv incidents, which city officials reported on record. No Russian Defense Ministry figure was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Oleshky Evacuees Reach Ukraine as Kyiv Declares the Mission a Success
items.lede: Zelensky said the group crossed in through the Chernihiv region and urged continued aid access to the Russian-held town, while no total headcount was released.

sections.text: Ukraine and Russia have observed a ceasefire around Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in Ukraine's Kherson region, since 03:00 Kyiv time on 27 October (02:00 CET) [28][29]. US First Lady Melania Trump brokered the pause [30][31], and lawmaker David Arakhamia said it runs until 22:59 Kyiv time on 1 November [32]. On Friday, Ukraine's human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets and Russia's ombudsman Yana Lantratova ran the joint mission [33][34][35]. Interfax, citing Russian TV channel Zvezda, said evacuees were taken to a temporary shelter in Simferopol, in occupied Crimea [36]. Lubinets had set a 14:00 local deadline for residents to leave [37][38]. On Friday evening, he reported no ceasefire violations in 87 hours [39]. On Saturday morning, Arakhamia said the final plane had landed in Gomel, Belarus [40]. By Saturday afternoon, Zelensky said the evacuees had crossed into Ukraine in the Chernihiv region [41]. He said he hopes humanitarian access to Oleshky will continue [41]. Kyrylo Budanov, head of the presidential office, said the mission succeeded and all sides kept their agreements [42].
Confidence is high that the evacuees reached Ukraine, because Zelensky and Budanov say so on record. The total headcount and the Simferopol detail from Russian state TV are not established.

items.title: Ukraine and Türkiye Agree to Work on Reviving the Black Sea Grain Corridor
items.lede: After meeting Zelensky in Istanbul, Erdoğan said Ankara will also take up safe Black Sea shipping with Moscow and called a deal a possible boost to peace efforts.

sections.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky made a working visit to Istanbul on 31 October at President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's invitation, as Turkish presidential communications head Burhanettin Duran announced on X beforehand [43][44]. Duran said the talks would cover bilateral cooperation, the war between Russia and Ukraine, and the security situation in the Black Sea [43][44]. Erdoğan received him at the Dolmabahçe presidential office, and the two leaders held one-on-one talks [45][46]. Turkish Defense Minister Yaşar Güler, intelligence chief İbrahim Kalın, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, and foreign intelligence head Rustem Umierov joined the delegation talks [45]. At a news conference afterward, Zelensky said he and Erdoğan agreed to work on restoring the Black Sea grain corridor [47]. Erdoğan said Türkiye would keep talking with both sides, including Russia, to restore safe shipping in the Black Sea [48]. Erdoğan also reaffirmed Türkiye's support for Ukraine's territorial integrity [48].

Confidence is high on the leaders' statements, which they made on record at a news conference reported by Ukrainian outlets and a Turkish outlet. No Russian response to the grain corridor plan was found by the cutoff.

theaters.heading: Sabotage, drones, cyber, disinformation, and espionage targeting European states

items.title: Belarusian Hackers Claim 23 Terabytes Stolen From Russia's Statistics Agency
items.lede: The agency denied any leak of protected data, but its main website stayed offline Sunday afternoon after hacker messages appeared on its portals.

sections.text: Russia's state statistics service, Rosstat, said its information resources faced targeted destructive cyberattacks from 29 October to 1 November [1]. Rosstat said its monitoring systems flagged the activity in time and found no database compromise or leak of protected data [1]. It said specialists and law enforcement were working to identify the attack vector and its sources [1]. Messages from the Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow appeared on Rosstat's main website and regional portals, the agency told RBC [2]. The hackers claimed they took 23 terabytes, including data on Russian war losses and documents marked for official use only [2]. The Moscow Times said the claims could not be independently verified [2]. Rosstat's main website was still down Sunday afternoon [2]. Both groups are banned in Russia as extremist, and they claimed a July 2025 attack on Aeroflot [2].

Confidence is high that Rosstat reported the attacks, based on its statement via Interfax and The Moscow Times. The 23-terabyte theft and the war-loss data rest only on the hackers' unverified claims.

items.title: Britain Flies Its Protector Drone at Home to Track a Russian Frigate
items.lede: The unarmed RAF aircraft gave Royal Navy ships over 10 hours of Channel coverage in October, a first that British media reported on Sunday.

sections.text: A British Royal Air Force Protector RG1 drone flew its first operational sorties in UK airspace, the UK Ministry of Defence said [3][4]. The unarmed aircraft gave the Royal Navy more than 10 hours of surveillance over the English Channel [3][4]. It supported the destroyer HMS Dauntless and the patrol ship HMS Tyne as they tracked the Russian frigate Neustrashimy [3]. The warships monitored the frigate and accompanying merchant ships through the Channel between 1 and 14 October [3]. Metro said the drone's surveillance ran from 14 to 16 October [4]. RAF helicopters also tracked a Russian intelligence-gathering ship and a Russian landing ship in the Channel, Metro reported [4]. The ministry did not say how many sorties the drone flew or which sensors it used [3]. No Russian response was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that Britain flew the Protector against the Russian frigate, which Defence Blog and Metro report from the UK Ministry of Defence. The exact sortie dates differ slightly between the two outlets.

items.title: Jersey Readies Measures Against a Third Evening of Airport Drone Incursions
items.lede: Officials met Sunday after drones blocked arrivals on two straight evenings, and police still had no suspect for the British Crown Dependency's disruption.

sections.text: Unauthorized drones flew in restricted airspace near Jersey Airport on Friday evening, disrupting flights from Britain to the British Crown Dependency [5]. The first report came at about 20:20 local time (21:20 CET), and further drone activity was reported until about 22:30 (23:30 CET) [6]. Jersey Police Inspector Rob McCallum said officers believed two or three drones had been in the restricted airspace [5]. On Saturday at 21:05 CET, the airport reported fresh drone disruption to inbound flights [7][8]. Three more flights into Jersey were canceled, on top of three on Friday [8]. Chief Minister Lyndon Farnham said Jersey was working with UK authorities and specialist agencies on counter-drone technology and better detection [8]. On Sunday, Jersey government officials and operational partners met to review the response to both evenings [9]. The government said it was making arrangements to reduce the risk of more disruption if drones return Sunday evening [9]. Police told islanders not to approach anyone they believe is flying a drone [9]. No operator, motive, or state link was named by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on both nights of disruption and the Sunday government review, which the BBC, Channel 103, and ITV reported from official statements. The drone count rests on one police estimate.

items.title: Russia-Linked Cargo Ship Leaves Gotland After Swedish Police Check Its Crew
items.lede: Sweden's police found nothing to remark on, and the vessel sailed south on Sunday while its operator's reported spy links went unconfirmed.
items.flag: FOLLOW UP TO PREVIOUS REPORT · single-source, unconfirmed

sections.text: Swedish police boarded a dry-cargo ship at a port on northern Gotland overnight into Saturday [10][11]. Border police checked the crew's travel documents, a Stockholm police spokesperson said [10]. She said everything looked fine and the check found nothing to remark on [10]. TV4 said the ship is over 80 meters long and belongs to a company previously investigated over Russian hybrid and spying operations [11]. TV4 sources said the crew are Russian citizens and the national special forces unit took part; police declined to confirm either [11]. TV4 said ships from the same company have been linked to drone alerts in other European countries [11]. The ship cast off on Sunday morning and was moving south along Gotland's coast, Kvartal reported, citing TV4 [12]. No ship name, arrest, or seizure was reported by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that Swedish police boarded the ship and checked crew papers, which SVT and TV4 report from a police spokesperson. The Russian crew, the special forces role, the company's history, and the departure rest on TV4 alone, the last relayed by Kvartal.

items.title: Romania Scrambles F-16 Jets and Closes Iași Airspace as Two Drones Approach
items.lede: Alerts hit six counties for about two and a half hours, and the Defense Ministry said only one of the two drones was confirmed to have left.

sections.text: Romania issued air-raid alerts in six eastern counties on Saturday evening after radar tracked two drones near the border with Moldova [13][14]. Radar first detected one target about 10 kilometers from the Moldovan border, the Defense Ministry said [14]. A second target then entered Romanian airspace without authorization from the direction of Moldova [14]. The first RO-Alert went to Iași county at 16:04 CET, followed by Neamț, Vaslui, Botoșani, Bacău, and Suceava [13]. Two F-16 jets and an IAR-330 helicopter took off, and two more F-16s later joined from Fetești air base [13]. Iași airspace was closed, and a flight from Eindhoven was diverted to Suceava [13][14]. The ministry said at 18:20 CET that one of the two drones had left Romanian airspace [13]. Alerts began lifting at 18:24 CET, and Iași airspace reopened [13]. Defense Minister Radu Oprea said the priority was protecting the population and national airspace [13]. No crash, damage, or injuries were reported by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the alerts, the Iași closure, and the diversion, which Euronews România and RO Times reported from Romania's Defense Ministry and Agerpres. The jet count rests on Euronews România alone.

items.title: Moldova Tracks Two Stray Drones Crossing Its Territory During Russian Strikes
items.lede: The second drone entered from Ukraine's Vinnytsia region and crossed the north in about 22 minutes, after the first had vanished from radar.

sections.text: An unauthorized drone entered Moldova's airspace on Saturday at 15:24 CET, Moldova's Air Operations Center said [15][16]. It came from the direction of Semionovca in Ukraine's Odesa region and headed toward Plopi in the Transnistrian region [15][16]. Moldova restricted airspace in the north at 15:46 CET and in the center at 15:52 CET [16]. The drone disappeared from radar near Țibirica in Călărași district at 15:54 CET [15][16]. Authorities reopened northern and central airspace at 16:14 CET after the drone left Moldovan airspace [15]. The Defense Ministry linked the incident to massive Russian attacks on Ukraine [15]. A second drone entered Moldova's airspace at 16:50 CET from the direction of Ukraine's Vinnytsia region, the Defense Ministry said [17]. It flew past Dondușeni and over three villages in Edineț district in northern Moldova [17]. The ministry said it left Moldovan airspace near Viișoara at 17:12 CET [17]. No damage, injuries, or drone type had been reported by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on both flight paths and the airspace closures, which Moldova's Defense Ministry published and MOLDPRES and TVR Moldova reported. The drones' type and origin were not officially named.

items.title: Swiss Arms Maker Says Fire Destroyed Its LBD 40 Production Site
items.lede: Bern prosecutors suspect arson at the Thun plant, which supplies French riot police, and an unverified video tied the attack to Gen Z protests.

sections.text: Swiss arms maker Brügger & Thomet told franceinfo on Sunday that a fire fully destroyed the part of its Thun building where it made and stored LBD 40 launchers [1]. French police use the 40 mm launchers during riots [1]. Bern cantonal police were alerted shortly after 03:10 on 29 October, and nobody was hurt [1]. Police quickly favored a criminal cause, and regional prosecutors appealed for witnesses [1]. The French ecology group Les Soulèvements de la Terre said it received a one-minute video claiming the attack [1]. The clip mentions Switzerland, France, and Germany with Gen Z, franceinfo reported [1]. The video's authenticity had not been established [1]. The company said it would not be intimidated [1].
Confidence is moderate. franceinfo is the only source read, citing the company, Bern police, and prosecutors. No Bern police or prosecutor statement was opened directly by the cutoff.

items.title: Spanish Judge Jails Alleged Blocus Ideologue After a Quiet Barcelona Saturday
items.lede: The 18-year-old is accused of driving a Telegram group that urged the 24 October looting, while police ID checks topped 2,000 on Saturday.

sections.text: Spain's Catalan police and Barcelona city police flooded downtown Barcelona on Saturday afternoon for the Blocus calls, El País reported [2]. The day passed without incidents, and police identified more than 2,000 people in about 10 cities, 1,440 of them in Barcelona [3]. Police took 12 minors carrying items such as balaclavas to a station for their protection until parents collected them [2]. Catalan police had set their top risk level, level 4, for only the second time for a protest since 2019 [4]. A court in Torrent on Saturday ordered the alleged Spanish founder of Blocus jailed after his Friday arrest in Valencia province [4]. Police also had four Telegram channels shut down [4]. The 24 October Barcelona looting ended with 133 arrests, 89 of them minors [2]. On Sunday, a Spanish judge jailed an 18-year-old arrested in Barcelona as an alleged Blocus ideologue, citing signs of conspiracy to cause public disorder [3]. Catalan police accused him of instigating and driving one of the Telegram groups that urged the looting [3].

Confidence is high on the deployment, the quiet day, and the jailing, reported by El País and consistent with RTVE and La Vanguardia. No official Catalan police statement on the jailing was found by the cutoff.

items.title: EU Commission Sides With Poland's Parliament in Constitutional Court Fight
items.lede: Justice Commissioner Michael McGrath backed Tusk's camp on appointing judges but stopped short of endorsing the suspension of the court's sidelined leadership.

sections.text: Riot police deployed on Friday evening at Poland's Constitutional Tribunal in Warsaw after Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska suspended its president, Bogdan Święczkowski, and vice-president, Bartłomiej Sochański, for one month [5]. The court wrote on X that everyone taking part was committing the crime of a coup d'état, as Law and Justice supporters, joined by leader Jarosław Kaczyński, protested outside [6][7]. Nawrocki canceled his Senegal trip in mid-flight and went to the court at about 01:00, where video showed scuffles with judges at the entrance [6][5]. Korwin-Piotrowska has called the court's general assembly for 3 November [5]. On Saturday morning, Nawrocki's chief of staff said the president would hold urgent consultations with government and opposition parties [8]. In a prime-time TV address on Saturday night, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk vowed to see the court overhaul through, saying some matters allow no compromise [9]. EU Justice Commissioner Michael McGrath told Politico Europe on Sunday that appointing the new judges lies with the Sejm, the lower house [10]. He did not endorse the suspension of the court's president and deputy [10].

Confidence is high on the suspension, the court's statement, and Tusk's address, reported by the BBC, El País, ANSA, and the Guardian. Politico Europe reported McGrath's remarks. No ruling on the suspension's legality was found by the cutoff.

items.title: French Prosecutors Open Attempted Murder Probe Into Firebombing of Gendarme
items.lede: The burned officer said about 10 in his unit were hurt in Saturday's clashes, which capped a day of 565 arrests.

sections.text: France's third Saturday of cost-of-living protests drew 320,000 people nationwide, including 70,000 in Paris, the Interior Ministry and Paris police said [11][12]. The Interior Ministry said police had arrested 565 people nationwide by 21:00 [12][13]. The Paris march kept to the outer boulevards after France's Conseil d'État canceled the Bastille–Nation route [11][14]. At the dispersal, police used tear gas and baton charges against groups throwing paving stones and a firebomb [11][13]. By 21:00, Paris police reported 79 arrests and five officers hurt, three of them burned by a firebomb [12]. The Interior Ministry said IGPN and IGGN watchdogs had 83 cases since mid-September student protests began, including a Reims marcher's shin seriously injured by a police grenade, franceinfo reported [15][16]. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez called the firebombing attempted murder [11][13]. Prosecutors opened an attempted-homicide investigation on Sunday [17]. The burned gendarme said about 10 in his company were hurt [17]. The prefecture's order n° 2026-01485 bars everyone from the Place de la République and Châtelet-Les Halles sectors from 23:00 to 06:00 on Saturday and Sunday nights [18][19]. A planned 0.8% riot insurance surcharge from 2027 still needs Conseil d'État validation [20].
Confidence is high on turnout, arrests, and the Paris clashes, per franceinfo, the Guardian, and RTBF with AFP. The 10 hurt gendarmes figure is one officer's account.

items.title: Spain's Renfe Orders Drivers to Slow Trains After Deadly Urda Crash
items.lede: An Adif incident log shows the LZB signaling system failed 23 minutes before Wednesday's collision, which killed 69 people on the Madrid–Seville high-speed line.

sections.text: Spain's state rail operator Renfe will order its more than 6,000 drivers to slow down sharply whenever the LZB train-protection system fails, El País reported [21]. A draft order caps speed at 40 km/h in such cases, and the paper said it could still change [21]. Renfe is drafting the final version with infrastructure manager Adif [21]. The crash near Urda, in Toledo province, killed 69 people on Wednesday, 28 October [21]. A Renfe AVE train hit a stationary Iryo train [22]. An Adif incident log opened at 08:30, 23 minutes before the crash, recorded a failure of the LZB control center at Urda [22]. It also noted power losses, downed phone lines, and intermittent data loss, El País reported [22]. The paper said drivers then received disjointed instructions from the Madrid-Atocha control center [22].
Confidence is moderate. Both reports come from El País, which cites Adif's incident log and a Renfe draft order it obtained. Neither Renfe nor Adif had publicly confirmed the order by the cutoff.

items.title: Dutch Police Arrest 34, Mostly Teens, in The Hague Over Gen Z Protest Calls
items.lede: Police said no major incidents occurred, though fireworks thrown at officers sent one to the hospital with possible hearing damage.

sections.text: Dutch riot police briefly cleared the Korte Voorhout in The Hague at about 15:15 on Saturday after youths ignored orders to move to the Malieveld, Omroep West reported [23]. Calls for a 'Gen Z protest' had spread on social media during the week, and shops in The Hague, Maastricht, and Amsterdam were boarded up [24]. The city had banned face coverings for Saturday [24]. Police also arrested several protesters in Delft [24]. Several hundred people, including ADO Den Haag soccer fans, gathered on the Plein and said they had come to protect the city [23]. The city extended an emergency order to the Malieveld and the central station area in the afternoon [23]. Maastricht police reported no incidents, and Amsterdam, Rotterdam, and Utrecht stayed quiet [24]. By evening, Dutch police said they had arrested 34 people in The Hague, mostly minors aged 15 to 18 from across the Netherlands [25]. One officer went to the hospital with possible hearing damage after illegal fireworks were thrown at police [25]. Mayor Jan van Zanen said heavy policing kept the situation under control [25].
Confidence is high on the arrests, the injury, and the emergency order, reported by NOS, Omroep West, and NU.nl and attributed to Dutch police and the mayor.

items.title: EU's Kallas Warns Putin's G20 Return Would Normalize War Crimes
items.lede: The EU foreign policy chief spoke after European officials refused to pose beside Russia's Sergei Lavrov at a G20 meeting in Atlanta.

sections.text: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on Saturday that Russian President Vladimir Putin's possible return to the G20 risks normalizing Russia's war crimes in Ukraine [26]. She spoke in a Bloomberg TV interview, Politico Europe reported [26]. The United States hosts the G20 leaders' summit in Florida in December, and Putin has not said whether he will attend [26]. At a G20 ministers' meeting in Atlanta, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio canceled the family photo after European officials refused to stand beside Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov [26]. Kallas called the U.S. sale of 500 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine very positive and urged tougher sanctions on Russia [26]. She also rejected reported Pentagon calls for NATO states to soften their criticism of the Kremlin [26].

Confidence is moderate. Politico Europe reported the remarks from a Bloomberg TV interview; the Bloomberg video was not checked. The EEAS press page showed her G20 remarks but no transcript of this interview.

items.title: Lawmaker Says Lithuania's Premier Should Quit Over Plagiarism in His Dissertation
items.lede: Dainius Gaižauskas said an early election would be acceptable, while Mindaugas Sinkevičius admits citation errors but defends the thesis's scientific value.

sections.text: Lithuanian lawmaker Dainius Gaižauskas of the Farmers and Greens Union told Lrytas TV on Sunday that Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius must resign, Elta reported via LRT [1]. He said an early election would be acceptable if it came to that [1]. An ethics commission at ISM University of Management and Economics found serious citation and attribution breaches, including plagiarism, in the dissertation [1]. The university ordered Sinkevičius to correct the work within six months [1]. Sinkevičius admitted the citation breaches but said the dissertation keeps its scientific value [1]. He said the ethics commission considered revoking his degree a disproportionate step [1].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one Elta report carried by LRT; the university's findings and the premier's statement were not read directly.

items.title: Lithuania's Anti-Graft Agency Finds No Sign Civic Group Sought Defense Contract Favors
items.lede: The Nemunas Dawn party had accused the Visuotinė gynyba association of pressuring politicians and the army, and the ethics watchdog will still review lobbying questions.

sections.text: Lithuania's Special Investigation Service (STT) found no data that donors or members of the Visuotinė gynyba association sought special terms in defense procurement, BNS reported via LRT [2]. Nemunas Dawn lawmakers took their complaint to the Prosecutor General's Office, which passed it to the STT [2]. The STT sent the possible lobbying questions to the Chief Official Ethics Commission (VTEK) [2]. VTEK chair Jolanta Bernotaitė said the commission will consider the STT material at its next meeting [2]. She said VTEK declined to open a probe based on a separate referral from the State Security Department, citing a lack of facts [2]. Association head Tomas Godliauskas earlier rejected the claims and said the group aims to boost public resilience [2].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one BNS report carried by LRT quoting agency statements; the STT and VTEK statements were not read directly.

items.title: Estonia's Social Democrats Name Ex-Diplomat Jonatan Vseviov as Their Prime Minister Candidate
items.lede: The former Foreign Ministry chief will lead the party list in Harju and Rapla counties for the 7 March 2027 parliamentary election.

sections.text: The council of Estonia's Social Democratic Party (SDE) endorsed Jonatan Vseviov on Sunday as its candidate for prime minister, ERR reported [3]. Vseviov stepped down as secretary general of the Foreign Ministry to run in the election [3]. Party leader Lauri Läänemets proposed the nomination and said support for the party has tripled since the 2023 election [3]. Vseviov called for a more ambitious foreign policy and a stronger Estonian voice in Europe [3]. He said Estonia cannot keep issues off the international agenda by keeping quiet [3].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one ERR report quoting the party leader and the candidate; no party statement or second outlet was read.

items.title: Lithuania Stops Taking Work and Study Permit Requests From Many Foreigners Already Inside
items.lede: Visitors on Schengen visas must now file through VFS Global centers abroad, and Belarusians can apply for work permits in Armenia and Georgia.

sections.text: Lithuania's new rules on temporary residence permits for work or bachelor's studies took effect Sunday, LRT reported, citing the Migration Department [4]. Foreigners who entered on a Schengen visa or another country's national visa can no longer file those requests inside Lithuania [4]. Only holders of a Lithuanian permit or national visa, an EU or Schengen residence permit, or visa-free status may still file in the country [4]. Others must apply at centers run by the outside contractor VFS Global [4]. The change does not apply to highly qualified workers [4]. Belarusian citizens can file work-permit requests at VFS Global offices in Armenia and Georgia [4].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one LRT report citing the Migration Department; the department's notice and the amended law were not read directly.

items.title: Estonia's President Picks Supreme Court Justice Oliver Kask as Chancellor of Justice
items.lede: Kask, a former election committee chair, vowed to keep the ombudsman office nonpolitical as Reform, EKRE, and the Social Democrats set their own tests.
items.flag: FOLLOW UP TO PREVIOUS REPORT · single-source, unconfirmed

sections.text: Estonian President Ülle Madise proposed to parliament on Saturday that Supreme Court Justice Oliver Kask become the next chancellor of justice, ERR reported [5]. Madise held the post until she took office as president earlier in October [5]. Kask was a Tallinn Circuit Court judge from 2004 to 2024 and joined the Supreme Court in September 2024 [5]. Parliament appoints the chancellor for seven years, and its party groups plan to meet Kask the week after next [6]. Kask told ERR the office must not be political and that political questions belong to parliament and the government [6]. He said he would focus first on social rights for people who struggle to defend themselves in court [6]. The Social Democrats want the chancellor to keep working on personal data protection [6]. EKRE said Kask must prove his independence and defend e-voting oversight [6]. ERR's English service reported Sunday that Kask once chaired Estonia's National Electoral Committee [7]. Reform lawmaker Madis Timpson said the chancellor should push for better laws, not more laws [7]. No vote date was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on three ERR reports quoting the president, the nominee, and party figures; no outlet outside ERR was read.

items.title: Lithuania's Cities Have Evacuation Routes but Lack Buses for Disabled Residents
items.lede: Only about 800 of more than 6,500 public shelters are adapted for people with disabilities, and 13 municipalities have none at all.

sections.text: Kaunas, Šiauliai, Panevėžys, and Marijampolė told the Elta news agency they have evacuation routes, assembly points, and vehicles planned, LRT reported [8]. Lithuania's national plan assumes about 75% of residents could leave on their own and 25% would need organized transport [8]. The plan requires evacuation within 72 hours of an official decision [8]. Kaunas and Marijampolė said their adapted vehicles would not carry all residents with disabilities at once [8]. Šiauliai said its fleet could move about 6,000 people in one trip [8]. In a separate LRT report, disability groups said shelter access is their biggest worry [9]. Data from the LT72 preparedness site show just over 800 of more than 6,500 shelters, about 12%, are adapted for people with disabilities, and 13 municipalities have none [9].
Confidence is moderate: the facts rest on two LRT reports, one relaying an Elta survey of city halls; the national plan and LT72 data were not read directly.

items.title: Serbian Observers Report Vote-Buying Claims in a Repeat Election Round
items.lede: CRTA monitors flagged isolated problems at 53 polling stations where 24,438 people could vote again in the 25 October snap parliamentary election.

sections.text: Serbia held repeat voting on Sunday at 53 polling stations in 24 cities and municipalities, N1 reported, citing the observer group CRTA [1]. The rerun is part of the 25 October snap parliamentary election [1]. CRTA said its observers recorded isolated cases of pressure on voters [1]. These included vote-buying, parallel voter lists, and third parties at or near polling stations [1]. CRTA said observers in Aleksinac heard claims of vote-buying for the list of Usame Zukorlić's SPP [1]. It said UV lamps were not used properly at some stations in Novi Pazar and Majdanpek [1]. No statement from the Republic Electoral Commission was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on CRTA's statement as relayed by N1; no electoral commission figures were read.

items.title: Bulgaria's Presidential Runoff Draws 19.33% Turnout by Midafternoon
items.lede: Participation is running ahead of the first round, while police logged 461 complaints, mostly about vote-buying; polls close at 19:00 CET, and no results are out.

sections.text: Bulgaria's Central Election Commission (CIK) said turnout in Sunday's presidential runoff was 19.33% at 16:00 Sofia time (15:00 CET) [2] [3]. At the same point in the first round, turnout was 16.04% [2]. Turnout was 6.11% at 11:00 Sofia time [4]. Sofia's 23rd electoral district had the highest rate at 16:00, at 29.21% [2]. Kardzhali had the lowest, at 9.84% [2]. The Interior Ministry said it had received 461 reports of suspected election violations by 14:30 Sofia time [5]. Of those, 318 concerned vote-buying and 49 concerned unlawful campaigning [5]. Police opened 10 criminal proceedings and detained 10 people [5]. The ministry said voting was proceeding normally [5]. Polls close at 20:00 Sofia time (19:00 CET), after the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the turnout figures, which come from CIK briefings reported by BTA and Banker.bg; the violation counts rest on the Interior Ministry's own statement via BTA.

items.title: Bulgaria Warns Ships of Drifting Containers Off Burgas After Drone Strike Sinking
items.lede: Four containers were spotted in the Black Sea on Sunday, days after maritime drones sank a cargo ship off Shabla and spilled part of its load.

sections.text: Bulgaria's Vessel Traffic Management and Information System (VTMIS) issued a navigational warning on Sunday about four containers drifting east of Burgas Bay, BTA reported [6]. The containers were sighted at four separate positions at 10:55 [6]. The warning told vessels to proceed with extreme caution [6]. On 28 October, three maritime drones struck a container ship about 21 nautical miles southeast of Shabla [6]. The ship sank around midnight, the Varna Regional Administration said [6]. Navy commander Rear Adm. Kiril Mihaylov said at the time that 20 of the 421 containers aboard had fallen overboard [6]. BTA did not say whether the four containers came from the sunken ship.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on the VTMIS warning as reported by BTA; no second outlet was checked by the cutoff.

items.title: Serbia's Central Bank Revokes Alta Bank's License Overnight
items.lede: The regulator also filed a criminal complaint against the lender and its officials, and insured deposits will be paid within seven business days after a court opens bankruptcy proceedings.

sections.text: The National Bank of Serbia revoked Alta Bank's operating license in a statement sent to the media at 02:25 CET on Saturday, Danas reported [7]. The central bank said the bank's financial condition had worsened significantly and depositors' interests were at risk [7]. A court will name the Deposit Insurance Agency receiver, and the agency will start paying insured deposits no later than seven business days after the Belgrade Commercial Court opens bankruptcy proceedings [7][8]. Four vice governors said they learned of the bank's true condition only at an emergency board session on Friday evening, N1 reported [9]. They said that condition differed sharply from the reports the bank had filed [9]. The organized crime prosecutor's office said it received a criminal complaint from the central bank against Alta Bank and several officials [9]. It said it had asked the central bank on 27 October for data on the bank's foreign transfers [9]. Deposit Insurance Agency director Ljubica Pantelić told Radio Belgrade on Saturday that the Belgrade Commercial Court should formally open bankruptcy proceedings on Monday [10][11].
Confidence is high on the license revocation and payout terms, from the central bank statement reported by Danas and N1. The National Bank of Serbia's own statement now opens and matches.

items.title: Albanian Police Fire Tear Gas as Tirana Protesters Throw Molotov Cocktails
items.lede: Police arrested three people after the 19th day of protests, as students kept opposition lawmakers at a distance from their rally.

sections.text: Protesters in Albania's capital, Tirana, threw volleys of Molotov cocktails at police on Saturday, Gazeta Express reported, citing Top Channel [12]. Police answered with tear gas and water cannon to disperse the crowd, and the area stayed tense [12] [13]. At a student protest outside the Education Ministry, the arrival of Democratic Party supporters and lawmakers set off a brief fight between two people, Kosovo Online reported, citing Koha [13]. Students said they wanted their movement to stay independent of parties [13]. They chanted "We are the opposition!" and "Rama to prison, Berisha to prison" [13]. Top Channel reported that three people were arrested and that police seized Molotov cocktails, Kosovo Online said [14]. Police said a masked group threw the stones and had been identified [14]. Clashes moved to the government building at about 16:30 and spread into nearby streets [14]. Prime Minister Edi Rama mocked the protesters on social media [14]. Democratic Party leader Sali Berisha did not join the march [14]. No police injury figures were found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the clashes, reported by Gazeta Express and Kosovo Online from Albanian broadcasters; the arrest count rests on Top Channel, and no full police statement was read.

items.title: Belgrade Prosecutors Find Only Copies in Sacks Dumped Outside a Serbian Town Hall
items.lede: Prosecutors see no grounds for a criminal case so far after residents reported shredded files outside the municipal offices of Zemun, a Belgrade district.

sections.text: Serbian prosecutors said 10 sacks of destroyed papers dumped outside Belgrade's Zemun municipality on 30 October held only discarded copies, Vijesti reported, citing Beta and Insajder [15]. The Third Basic Public Prosecutor's Office said the originals remain in the municipal offices [15]. A prosecutor and Zemun police went to the scene after residents complained [15]. They checked all 10 sacks and security camera footage [15]. They interviewed 21 people, including the municipality's president and its head of public procurement [15]. Prosecutors said they will act if new evidence emerges [15].
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on the prosecutors' statement as relayed by Beta and Insajder through Vijesti; the statement itself was not read.

items.title: Georgia Says Russian Forces Freed a Citizen Detained Near the South Ossetia Line
items.lede: The State Security Service said the man held near Bershueti in Gori Municipality is back in government-controlled territory after EU monitors' hotline was used.

sections.text: Georgia's State Security Service (SSG) said on Sunday that a Georgian citizen detained by Russian forces near the village of Bershueti has been released, Interpressnews reported [1]. Bershueti is in Gori Municipality, near the line with Russian-occupied South Ossetia [1]. The SSG statement dated the case to 31 October and said the man is now in territory controlled by the central government [1]. The SSG said it used all available mechanisms, including the hotline run by the EU Monitoring Mission in Georgia (EUMM) [1]. It said it is working to free all Georgian citizens held in the occupied territories [1]. The statement did not name the man or say how long he was held.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on the SSG statement as relayed by Interpressnews; no EUMM or Tskhinvali comment was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Armenia's Foreign Minister Pitches Peace and Transit Links to Gulf Forum in Bahrain
items.lede: Ararat Mirzoyan told the Manama Dialogue's closing session that Armenia has chosen peace and that the TRIPP route will link East and West.

sections.text: Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan met Gulf Cooperation Council Secretary-General Jasem Albudaiwi in Manama, Bahrain, Report.az reported [2]. Mirzoyan posted about the meeting on X on 31 October [2]. He said they discussed closer institutional cooperation and economic ties [2]. They also discussed regional transport links and the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity project [2]. They discussed further institutionalizing peace between Armenia and Azerbaijan and the situation in the Middle East [2]. On 1 November, Mirzoyan addressed the closing plenary of the Manama Dialogue, Armenia's Foreign Ministry said [3]. Bahrain's foreign minister and UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash also spoke on the panel [3]. Mirzoyan called the August 2025 Washington summit a historic milestone toward peace with Azerbaijan [3]. He said the TRIPP project would bring rail, power, fiber optic, and oil and gas links across Armenia [3].
Confidence is high, as both accounts come from the minister's own post and his ministry's published speech text; no Azerbaijani reaction was found by the cutoff.

items.title: Georgians March in Tbilisi on the 703rd Day of Pro-EU Protests
items.lede: Relatives of jailed demonstrators joined the rally and aimed its main slogan at Bidzina Ivanishvili, the billionaire founder of the ruling Georgian Dream party.

sections.text: Protesters in Georgia held their weekly Saturday march in the capital, Tbilisi, on 31 October, JAMnews reported [4]. It marked 703 days of continuous pro-European protests [4]. The main slogan was "Georgia against Ivanishvili" [4]. Family members of activists detained at earlier rallies joined the march [4]. Protesters demand early elections, the release of political prisoners, and repeal of laws passed by Georgian Dream [4]. JAMnews counts about 150 prisoners of conscience in Georgia [4]. No arrests or clashes were reported by the cutoff, and no turnout figure was found.
Confidence is moderate: the account rests on JAMnews photo coverage; no police statement or second outlet was read.

items.title: Azerbaijani Media Accuse Turkish Outlets of Passing Off an Old Aliyev Speech
items.lede: Baku-based outlets say Turkish papers presented a 2020 victory address as a new warning to Ankara, feeding talk of a rift between the allies.

sections.text: Azerbaijan's Report.az and Oxu.Az accused some Turkish media of spreading a misleading video of President Ilham Aliyev [5]. An unofficial TikTok account posted footage of Aliyev with audio from his 10 November 2020 address on the Karabakh war [5]. Turkish papers Milli Gazete and Sonsöz presented it as a post from Aliyev's official account [5]. Social media users then asked whether it was a message to Turkey [5]. Oxu.Az said Aliyev has no official TikTok account [5]. It urged the outlets to correct their reports [5]. No Turkish response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate on the dispute, which rests on Report.az relaying Oxu.Az; the Turkish reports were not read.

items.title: Germany's New Military Combat Helicopters Will Fly Without Weapons for Now, Spiegel Says
items.lede: The report is a setback for Defense Minister Boris Pistorius, who is buying ready-made equipment to rebuild the Bundeswehr quickly.

sections.text: Germany's new military combat helicopters can fly but will not be able to fire weapons for the foreseeable future, Der Spiegel reported Sunday [1]. The magazine cited its own information [1]. Defense Minister Boris Pistorius wants to rearm the Bundeswehr at record speed [1]. His plan relies on weapons already on the market rather than new designs [1]. Spiegel said the helicopter purchase was one of the first showcase projects of that approach [1]. It said the plan did not work in this case [1].
Confidence is low because only Spiegel has reported this, and only the article's summary was available behind its paywall. The defense ministry had not commented in the material seen by the cutoff.

items.title: Germany Misses Its Legal Gas Storage Target With Tanks About 61% Full
items.lede: The government and the network regulator say winter supply is safe thanks to new import terminals, while a Greens lawmaker says there is no safety buffer.

sections.text: Germany's gas storage sites were about 61.2% full on Sunday, short of the 70% average the law requires by 1 November, according to European AGSI data [2]. The economy ministry said winter supply remains secure [2]. Federal Network Agency head Klaus Müller said meeting the storage targets is no longer essential for secure supply [2] [3]. He pointed to Germany's liquefied natural gas terminals [2]. The agency said it sees no need to act [2]. Greens energy lawmaker Michael Kellner accused Economy Minister Katherina Reiche of poor planning [2]. He said storage levels are the lowest ever and leave no safety buffer [2]. An industry association warned of possible shortages [3]. Tim Kehler of the gas and water industry association said missing the target brings no penalties [2].

Confidence is high on the fill level and official statements, reported by tagesschau and Deutschlandfunk. The fill figure comes from AGSI data as cited by tagesschau and was not checked against the platform directly.

items.title: German Prosecutor Andrés Ritter Takes Charge of the EU's Fraud Prosecution Office
items.lede: The former deputy chief now leads the Luxembourg agency that pursues customs and tax fraud against the bloc's budget.

sections.text: German prosecutor Andrés Ritter became European Chief Prosecutor on Sunday [4]. His seven-year term at the European Public Prosecutor's Office in Luxembourg began on 1 November [4]. EU governments and the European Parliament approved his nomination in the spring [4]. Ritter was deputy to Romania's Laura Kövesi, who led the office for seven years [4]. He earlier ran an economic and cybercrime prosecutor's office in Rostock, in Germany's Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania state [4]. The office investigates fraud against the EU budget [4]. Its investigators had a record 3,602 active cases at the end of 2025, with estimated damage of about 67 billion euros [4]. Most involve customs and value-added tax fraud [4]. Twenty-five EU countries take part [4].

Confidence is high on the appointment, which DW reported with dpa photos and which follows a confirmation process completed in the spring. The case figures come from the office's annual report as cited by DW.

items.title: Frankfurt Police Report 54 Arrests and 100 Officers Hurt After Germany's Gen Z Rallies
items.lede: Police now blame most of the looting on youths with no clear political motive, and Germany's Social Democrats want a national summit on schools.

sections.text: Germany's 'Gen Z regelt' youth rallies in more than 30 cities stayed mostly peaceful on Saturday [5] [6]. Frankfurt police said Sunday they had made 54 arrests and recorded 87 criminal complaints [7]. About 100 officers were hurt, and five stores were looted [7] [8]. Hesse Interior Minister Roman Poseck said one officer was seriously injured [8]. Police blamed the later looting mainly on known groups of young men who meet downtown on weekends, many with immigrant backgrounds [7]. Police President Stefan Müller said they showed no political motive [7]. Poseck said those arrested are 13 to 29 years old and mostly German citizens [7]. On Saturday, he had blamed about 100 violent left-wing extremists [9]. In Baden-Württemberg, the state interior ministry reported nine officers hurt and seven people detained among almost 15,000 marchers [10]. Federal Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt blamed "violent left-wing groups" and "troublemakers from the migrant milieu" and called for tough sentences [11]. The SPD parliamentary group called for a national education summit [12]. The organizers distanced themselves from the violence and plan new protests on 20 November [13] [6].
Confidence is high on the Frankfurt figures, which come from a police and ministry press conference reported by tagesschau and Deutschlandfunk. No nationwide arrest count was available by the cutoff.

items.title: Warning Strikes Begin at Midnight in Germany's Metal Industry Pay Dispute
items.lede: Night shifts walked out in Andernach, Munich, and Hildesheim, and the union plans to spread the action across the country next week.

sections.text: Germany's IG Metall union began warning strikes in the metal and electrical industry just after midnight, when a no-strike obligation expired [14] [15]. About 300 night-shift workers at thyssenkrupp Rasselstein in Andernach, Rhineland-Palatinate, stopped work and rallied at the plant gate [14] [15]. A walkout also began at RF360 Europe/Qualcomm, a mobile-phone parts supplier in Munich [15]. Regional union leader Joerg Koehlinger called the Andernach walkout the start of a massive strike phase [14]. The union said the strikes will spread across Germany in the coming days [16] [15]. The union had said a large Bavarian carmaker will be hit for the first time on Monday [17]. IG Metall wants a 5% raise over 12 months and job guarantees for about 3.7 million workers [15] [16]. Employers have offered a one-time payment next year and a 1.3% raise in 2028 [16] [14]. Night-shift workers also walked out at auto supplier KSM Castings in Hildesheim, Lower Saxony [18]. Union leader Christiane Benner has promised strong warning strikes [18].
Confidence is high on the start of the strikes, reported by tagesschau, SWR, BR24, and Deutschlandfunk from union statements. Turnout figures beyond Andernach were not available by the cutoff.

items.title: Berlin's Left Party Votes to Open Coalition Talks With Greens and SPD
items.lede: Negotiations on a Left-led government for Germany's capital start Monday, and parliamentary leader Elif Eralp accused Chancellor Merz of pressuring her partners.

sections.text: The Left Party in Berlin, Germany's capital, voted at a state party congress Saturday to open coalition talks with the Greens and the SPD [19] [20]. A clear majority of delegates backed the move [19] [20]. The Greens and the SPD had already agreed to talks [19] [20]. Negotiations are set to begin Monday, six weeks after the Berlin election [19]. The planned Left-led alliance has been controversial across Germany for weeks [19]. Left parliamentary leader Elif Eralp told delegates she will not give up her bid to become Berlin's mayor [19]. She accused Chancellor Friedrich Merz of trying to blackmail the Greens and the SPD into blocking the coalition [19].
Confidence is high. tagesschau and Deutschlandfunk both report the vote. No response from Merz to Eralp's accusation was found by the cutoff.
